chapter_theme: Light (ஒளி): the Lord is light, the source of the light of sun, moon and fire, which are his eyes, and of the five elements; he stays within the body and mind as an inner light that gives life and drives out the darkness of maya and bonds. To know the light is to find form and light one, and those it reaches are joined to him as fragrance to a flower.
structure_note: The verses play on ஒளி in nearly every line, often with the rhyming pair விளங்கொளி, துளங்கொளி, வளங்கொளி, களங்கொளி. Knowing the light (2681); the Lord's light in the cosmos, its lamps and elements (2682 to 2686); the light within body, soul and mind (2687 to 2691); the removal of darkness (2692 to 2696); and the Lord who alone is (2697). The grouping is mine.

2681.reading: If one knows the light, there are form and light; if one knows light as form, it is form; if one knows the form of the light, it is light alone; and he stayed with one as the light itself melted.
2681.nuance: A riddle built on ஒளி and உரு (form). It is commonly taken to say that the Lord is known first as form and light, then as light alone. ஒளியும் உருக (the light melting) may also be read as the light and the knower dissolving together.

2682.reading: The eight worlds become easy to reach, the wide light spreads so that darkness leaves without trace, and making the light of day in that lotus, our Lord stayed there shining with a light that outdoes all.
2682.nuance: அத்தாமரை (that lotus) is commonly taken as the heart lotus, so the light of the worlds is also the light within. இகல் ஒளி is a light that rivals or surpasses.

2683.reading: Fire with its bright light, the sun of spreading rays and the moon received their wavering light by the grace of that light; the rich light they received is the great light, which is other, and making light in the throat he stayed mingled with them.
2683.nuance: விரிகதிர் சோமன் may be 'the sun with spreading rays and the moon' or only 'the moon of spreading rays'. களங்கொளி may be the light of Siva's dark throat or simply 'light in its place'. The verse distinguishes the great light from the lights it lends.

2684.reading: Isan of young light has no birth at all; the wavering-lit sun and moon are his eyes, the rich-lit fire is the other eye in his forehead, and this is the true body that makes light shine.
2684.nuance: Sun, moon and fire as Siva's three eyes is standard Saiva iconography. மெய்காயம் (the true body) may be the Lord's body of light, or the yogi's body in which sun, moon and fire are the breaths and the inner fire.

2685.reading: Light above, and below it the wind that dwells there; fire of milky light; space spread out as light; water making light; in the one long sky the five lights above become one light.
2685.nuance: The five are the elements, each called a light, gathered into one; earth is not named unless மேல் ஒளி (light above) stands for it. The order and grouping are unclear.

2686.reading: The flashing pure light, the excellent red light, knowledge spoken of spreading as the supreme light, the six lights joined: by pure words said daily, the light matches the way one has contemplated it.
2686.nuance: The six lights (ஆறு ஒளி) may be the lights of the six adharas or the colours named in the verse; they are not listed. தூய்மொழி (pure word) is taken as mantra. The last line says the light answers to meditation.

2687.reading: The shining light, hiding itself as the light of lightning, the wavering light, always speaks of Isan; the light in the heart, standing in the flesh, gives life, and as that rich light he pervades everything.
2687.nuance: The rhyming light-words make the syntax loose: whether விளங்கொளி, துளங்கொளி and வளங்கொளி are three lights or one under three names is not clear. The verse places the life-giving light inside the body.

2688.reading: That shining light and that darkness both abide in him; he is the wavering light and the light even of those who worship; to take as nectar the poison that came from the salt sea is the intent of Isan with the shining throat.
2688.nuance: The last two lines recall Siva swallowing the poison from the churned sea, which stayed in his throat. அளங்கொளி ஆரமுதாக நஞ்சு ஆரும் can be read in several ways; I take அளம் as the salt sea. That light and darkness both abide in him is said, not explained.

2689.reading: Whatever light moves is the light of Isan; what is like a shining light is the abiding Shakti of grace; three shining lights appear as spreading flames, and within the heart's light he gathers into one.
2689.nuance: The three lights are taken as sun, moon and fire, as in 2684. தூங்கருட் சத்தி may be the grace-Shakti who abides or who hangs over all. The last word ஒருங்கிகின்றானே looks corrupt (see source_issues).

2690.reading: The light within me is the soul that stands there; the great gem's flame that stood as rich light, flashing as shining light and subsiding into the sky, he stood as rich light in the gathering.
2690.nuance: உலங்கொளி is unclear: perhaps உளங்கொளி, the heart's light, as in 2689. மாமணிச் சோதி (the great gem's flame) is the Lord. ஆயத்துள் (in the gathering, or in what has come to be) is unclear.

2691.reading: The strange one who stands as shining light dwells where the hanging darkness does not reach within the wavering light and its bonds; as the brow-eyed one dances the dance of darkness, he stands as one with the shining light in the inner mind.
2691.nuance: விகிர்தன் (the strange or different one) and கண்ணுதல் (forehead-eyed) are names of Siva. களங்கிருள் நட்டம் may be the dance in the dark of dissolution. The syntax of line 2 is loose.

2692.reading: In the message carried to her of the flowered dark tresses, the primal supreme with the Lord of the immortals, the light and the pure light beyond the cosmic egg: this is how, rightly, the good darkness was removed.
2692.nuance: The verse is very obscure. போனவர் தூது (the message of the one who went) and பரத்தை might recall a story of the Lord going as a messenger to a woman, but that would be a guess and I do not adopt it. நல்லிருள் (good darkness) is a puzzling phrase.

2693.reading: Saying 'it is' and 'it is not' is the way of this world; is there a supreme goal of which it is said 'it was not before'? People have not seen it; if they come to the meaning seen, there is no gap, and within it is the lamp's light.
2693.nuance: The verse sets the world's arguments of existence and non-existence against an inner seeing that leaves no gap. விண்டு இல்லை may be 'no split' or 'not spoken'. Who has 'seen the meaning' (கண்ட கருத்து) is not said: perhaps the sages.

2694.reading: The bright light that rose to touch the flame is there, Isan, the sun of a vision that spreads; if the dense darkness of maya is cast off, it comes by the renunciation of the world that clings to the body.
2694.nuance: The last line can also be read as 'it becomes the renunciant's, in this embodied world'. The sun here is an image of the Lord's light dispelling maya's darkness.

2695.reading: The first Lord, with a holy body of shining coral and white ash, gracious coral and fine gold, of coral joy: the black darkness gone, Isan stood with me in coral light.
2695.nuance: பவளம் (coral, red) recurs in every line for Siva's red body under white ash. The verse ends in the first person: the light stands with the speaker.

2696.reading: Isan stood, the gods stood, and with no ground to stand on they are bewildered and wear away; when the bonds become one and old karma's hold ends, it is like a flower and its single fragrance.
2696.nuance: பாசம் ஒன்றாக (the bonds becoming one) is unclear: perhaps the bonds gathering into one and falling away together. The flower and its single scent is an image of the soul and the Lord inseparable.

2697.reading: He alone is, the chief among them; approach him as the one who alone is; he is like the sky, and in this vast dark world, praising him is possible as he stands as light.
2697.nuance: பானாய் may be 'as light' (from பா, light, or பானு, the sun) or 'as a vessel'. மாயிரு ஞாலம் may be the great dark world or simply the great wide world.

links.note: Both give Siva three eyes that are three lights: here sun, moon and the forehead fire, in 2774 the three eyes in the dancer's body whose limbs are space and the eight directions.

Both use light driving out darkness: in the Naladiyar austerity drives out sin as a lamp does darkness, and evil returns when good deeds run out like a lamp's oil; in Tirumular the Lord's light casts off maya's darkness through renunciation, with no word of its return.

2683 says fire, sun and moon received their wavering light by the grace of that light, and that the great light is other (பேரொளி வேறு). Thiruppugazh 1111 asks for an inner vision of a ground of light that sun and moon do not reach (சூரியனுடன் சோமன் ... அண்டாத சோதி), a lotus of light joined like flower and fragrance. Both set the Lord's light apart from the lights of the sky; the Thiruppugazh makes it a place the devotee asks to enter.

2686 lists the lights and says that, by pure words recited daily, the light matches the way one has contemplated it (உன்னியவாறு ஒளி ஒத்தது). Kural 666 says people obtain what they have thought of as they thought of it, if they are firm (எண்ணிய எண்ணியாங்கு எய்துப). The same logic, that the result takes the shape of the steady thought behind it, governs the yogi's inner light in one and worldly undertakings in the other.

2688 says it is the intent of Isan to take as nectar the poison that came from the salt sea (அளங்கொளி ஆரமுதாக நஞ்சாரும்). Kural 580 says those who want a refinement worth loving drink poison though they see it poured (பெயக்கண்டும் நஞ்சுண்டு அமைவர்). Both make knowingly swallowing poison the mark of a larger nature, in the god's cosmic act and in the courtesy of a cultivated man.

2693 says that saying 'it is' and 'it is not' (உண்டில்லை என்னும்) is the way of this world, and asks after a supreme goal of which 'it was not before' cannot be said. Kural 336 says this world's greatness is that one who was here yesterday is not today (நெருநல் உளனொருவன் இன்றில்லை). On the reading that 2693's 'is and is not' is the world's transience, the Kural gives the plain fact and the Tirumanthiram sets against it the light within that has no gap.

2694 says Isan is the sun of a spreading vision (படருறு காட்சிப் பகலவன்), and that the dense darkness of maya (மாயையின் ஆரிருள்) is cast off by renouncing the world that clings to the body. Kural 352 says that for those of stainless sight who have left confusion, it removes darkness and brings joy (இருள்நீங்கி இன்பம் பயக்கும் மருள்நீங்கி மாசறு காட்சியவர்க்கு). Both tie the ending of darkness to a clear seeing; the Tirumanthiram names that seeing as the Lord himself and adds renunciation as its condition.

2695 has Isan with a holy body of shining coral and white ash, and ends that with the black darkness gone he stood with the poet in coral light (காரிருள் நீங்கி ஒளிபவளத்து என்னோடு ஈசன் நின்றானே). 114 says Nandi cut away the verdigris, showed a light no tarnish touches and set coral in crystal (பளிங்கிற் பவளம் பதித்தான்). In both the coral is the Lord's presence shown once the darkness or stain is removed; in 114 the crystal is the cleansed soul that holds it.

2696 says that when the bonds become one and old karma's hold ends, it is like a flower and its single fragrance (வாசம் ஒன்றா மலர் போன்றது). 2829 says that as the water lily's form, colour, bright fragrance and beauty stand together (உருஉற்பல நிறம் ஒண்மணம் சோபை), so the soul stands merged in the Supreme. Both use a flower and its scent for the soul's union, inseparable but not erased.

2697 says he alone is and is the chief among them (தானே யிருக்கும் அவற்றில் தலைவனும்), to be approached as the one who alone is. 2967 runs the same anaphora, he himself stands as directions, gods, body, life and tattvas, and ends that he himself is the Lord in the world (தானே உலகில் தலைவனும் ஆமே). The two say the same thing in nearly the same words; 2967 spells out what the 'all' is over which he alone is chief.

source_issues: 2689: line 4 ends ஒருங்கிகின் றானே, probably a misprint for ஒருங்கிநின் றானே.
2690 line 1 (உலங்கொளி) may be a misreading of உளங்கொளி; 2692 is obscure throughout and may be corrupt.
